Thought: I need to determine which amino acid is important for ionic bonding in drug binding. Let me analyze each option:

Ionic bonding involves the attraction between oppositely charged ions. For an amino acid to participate in ionic bonding, it would need to have a charged side chain.

A. Aspartate: Has a negatively charged carboxyl group in its side chain at physiological pH. This can form ionic bonds with positively charged groups.
B. Glycine: Has only a hydrogen atom as its side chain, so it cannot participate in ionic bonding.
C. Serine: Has a hydroxyl group in its side chain, which can participate in hydrogen bonding but not ionic bonding.
D. Valine: Has a hydrophobic side chain (isopropyl group) that cannot form ionic bonds.

Among these options, only aspartate has a charged side chain that can participate in ionic bonding. The negative charge on aspartate can interact with positively charged groups on drugs through ionic bonds.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]A[/ANSWER]
